argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower certification position than an unconditional compliance claim. Aggregate readiness is met, no severity-one rehearsal incidents are recorded, and staged rollout, rollback, and monitoring are in place. The same record also shows the HR benefits enrollment segment remains below target and exposed, and the draft risk acceptance is neither approved nor specific to that exposure. Under the stated policy, those controls do not replace disclosure. The supportable position is therefore to treat certification as acceptable only if it is explicitly conditioned on pre-launch model-card disclosure of the known HR benefits enrollment limitation and deployment monitoring, rather than treating rollout controls alone as sufficient.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to justify this position. The narrow requested treatment preserves the already-supported launch-readiness finding while aligning the certification basis to the policy requirement for disclosure.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not bar certification in all cases where a material limitation exists; it requires that the limitation be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Here, approved risk acceptance is not in evidence, and the exposed named use case remains in scope, so rollback, dashboards, monitoring, and a 9% rollout cannot carry the governance burden by themselves. The policy-compliant path available on this record is qualified certification tied to explicit disclosure and monitoring.
concessions: The current record does not support an unconditional finding that certification is already compliant as-is.
The current record does not show approved risk acceptance for the exposed HR benefits enrollment weakness.
The current record does not support treating rollout controls and monitoring alone as a substitute for disclosure.
